newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore fuel oil trades after 25 percent fall.
newsitem.headline: Singapore fuel oil trades after 25 percent fall.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil traded in the Singapore cash market on Wednesday at $93.00 per tonne, representing a $31 drop from the last deal done in December 30, traders said.
Fuel oil prices have plunged a dramatic 25 percent since the start of the year as prompt supplies flooded the market and China stopped buying ahead of Chinese New Year.
Traders said 20,000-tonne cargo for lifting fob Singapore February 17-21 was sold by the local office of British Petroleum & Co Plc to the local office of Dutch trader Vitol, industry sources said.
Fuel oil last traded in Singapore's cash market on December 30 at $124.00 per tonne, for January 14-18 cargo, between a U.S. major and a local trader.
Trade assessments for the price of fuel oil have dropped sharply in recent weeks, but traders said nothing had traded in 1997 until earlier on Wednesday.
